Add support for `CODEX_AUTH_HOME`

The goal is to be able to differenciate `CODEX_HOME` from `CODEX_AUTH_HOME` for this kind of use-case:
* I need to be able to spawn an agent with `codex exec` that is in pure read-only with no internet access
* with only the CLI, I can't disable the custom rules in `CODEX_HOME/rules`
* so I need to spawn the `codex exec` with a custom `CODEX_HOME`
* but copying the auth is a bad idea and it does not even work if the user uses keyring

Having the possibility to point to the original codex home for `CODEX_AUTH_HOME` fixes this issue

This is to be used internally only, we shouldn't advertise this feature and I don't think it makes sense for users

items.body:
## Why

Fixes #17954.

Manual user shell commands such as `!sleep 10` run as their own turn lifecycle. While that command is running, submitting a follow-up like `hi` currently attempts to steer the active turn. Because user shell turns were classified as regular tasks, core accepted the steer into turn pending input even though the user shell task never drives the regular model-turn loop that consumes pending input. The result is a stuck-looking TUI after the shell command exits, and pressing Esc can make the session feel locked.

## What Changed

This change classifies standalone user shell command turns as non-steerable:

- Adds `TaskKind::UserShell` for `UserShellCommandTask`.
- Rejects `turn/start` / `turn/steer` attempts against user shell turns with `ActiveTurnNotSteerable { turnKind: userShell }`.
- Updates app-server protocol schemas and generated TypeScript so clients can represent the new turn kind.
- Extends turn-steer analytics rejection reasons for user shell turns.
- Adds TUI regression coverage showing that a follow-up submitted during a user shell turn is queued and submitted after the shell turn completes.

## Tradeoffs

The alternative would be to make user shell turns truly steerable by draining pending input after the command completes and then running a regular model continuation in the same turn. That would preserve the idea that follow-ups submitted during active work are same-turn steers, but it would also make `!cmd` a hybrid "run a local command, then maybe continue with the model" lifecycle.

That steerable approach has a few complications:

- The user shell command output would need to be persisted and ordered before the pending user input is sent to the model.
- User-prompt hooks, telemetry, cancellation, and `TurnComplete` behavior would need to be shared carefully with `RegularTask` instead of copied.
- Failed, timed-out, or interrupted manual commands would need explicit semantics for whether queued steers should still run.
- The turn duration and completion notification would include the manual shell wait plus any model continuation, which changes the mental model of `!` commands.

This PR chooses the smaller behavior change: keep `!` commands standalone, reject same-turn steering for them, and rely on existing TUI retry logic to send the user's follow-up as the next normal turn after the shell command completes.

## App-Server Client Risk

This is an additive protocol change to `NonSteerableTurnKind`. App-server clients that handle `ActiveTurnNotSteerable` generically should continue to work and can queue/retry the submitted follow-up after the current turn completes.

Clients that exhaustively match the old `review | compact` `turnKind` set will need to update for the new `userShell` value. Until updated, those clients may show a generic error, fail exhaustive type checks after regenerating schema bindings, or drop the follow-up instead of retrying it.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p codex-core steer_input_rejects_non_regular_turns`
- `cargo test -p codex-tui user_shell_steer_rejection_queues_follow_up_until_shell_turn_completes`
- `cargo test -p codex-app-server-protocol codex_error_info_serializes_active_turn_not_steerable_turn_kind_in_camel_case`
- `cargo test -p codex-protocol active_turn_not_steerable_error_does_not_affect_turn_status`
- `just write-app-server-schema`
- `just fix -p codex-core -p codex-tui -p codex-app-server-protocol -p codex-app-server -p codex-analytics -p codex-protocol`
items.title: Treat user shell turns as non-steerable

items.body:
## Summary

Fixes #17954.

The TUI already treats composer text submitted while a task is running as a pending steer. That works for normal agent turns because the pending steer is removed when the server commits the matching user message item. Standalone `!` shell commands can use the same task-running path, but they may finish without ever acknowledging the pending steer, leaving the TUI with no queued follow-up to submit after the shell turn ends.

This keeps the fix local to the TUI and avoids adding app-server or core task semantics. When a live turn completes or errors with unacknowledged pending steers, the TUI now moves those steers into the existing rejected-steer/follow-up queue and lets the existing queued-input drain submit the next user turn. Replay reconciliation preserves each pending steer's owning turn id, so replayed completions, committed user-message items, interruptions, failures, and non-retry errors mutate restored pending input only when they match that owner, while non-stale replayed terminal events still clear stale local running state.

## Changes

- Drain unacknowledged `pending_steers` into the existing follow-up queue when a live turn ends before the steer is acknowledged.
- Reuse the existing queued-input submission path instead of tracking standalone shell turns.
- Preserve per-steer turn ids across thread input capture/restore.
- Keep pending-steer acknowledgement tied to the owning turn, including replayed committed user-message items for the restored active turn.
- Ignore stale replayed terminal/error/user-message events for pending-input mutation when they belong to historical turns.
- Record replayed in-progress turns as active so restored running state can be reconciled later.
- Restore pending input for replayed interrupted/failed active turns, and finalize non-stale replayed terminal/error events so the TUI does not stay stuck running when completion replay is incomplete.
- Add focused regression coverage for retrying an unacknowledged pending steer after turn completion and for turn-scoped replay safety.

## Tradeoffs

Making standalone user shell commands non-steerable would also avoid the stuck pending-steer state, but it would require lower layers to encode a TUI-specific distinction or require app-server clients to adapt to a new interpretation of user-command turns. Keeping user commands steerable preserves the current app-server/core behavior and should not require updates from other app-server clients, including the Codex app.

The main risk with the TUI-local approach is accidentally retrying input that was accepted but never acknowledged before turn completion. The TUI already treats committed user message items as the source of truth for clearing `pending_steers`, so this change leans on that acknowledgement path and uses restored per-steer turn ids during replay instead of adding another shell-specific state machine.
items.title: TUI: retry unacknowledged pending steers after turn completion

## Summary

A writable workspace with no `.git` at startup could run `git init` inside Linux bubblewrap and create git metadata outside the intended protected path set. This change closes that path without adding path specific mount cleanup.

Bugcrowd submission: linked from BUGB 15632

## Root Cause

The shared policy only protects `.git` after it exists. Linux bubblewrap needs to reserve the missing top level `.git` path for the active workspace root before the sandboxed command runs. Bubblewrap can materialize a host side mount target for that reservation, so the helper now removes only the synthetic empty target after bubblewrap exits.

## Scope

This PR touches four files.

1. `bwrap.rs` adds the missing top level `.git` reservation only for the active workspace root. Missing protected mount targets now share one read only tmpfs mask and cleanup helper, so `.git`, `.codex`, and future missing protected paths use the same handling.
2. `linux_run_main.rs` keeps the normal exec path when no cleanup is needed, runs bubblewrap through a child helper only when synthetic mount target cleanup is required, and treats a failed proc probe as a reason to retry without proc.
3. `linux_run_main_tests.rs` proves cleanup removes an empty synthetic target and preserves real git metadata.
4. `landlock.rs` adds a Linux regression test that proves `git init` is blocked while ordinary writable files still work.

## Validation

1. Local project format passed.
2. Local cargo format check passed.
3. Local Linux sandbox clippy passed.
4. Local Linux sandbox crate test passed on macOS, with Linux tests compiled out on this host.
5. Local whitespace diff check passed.

Addresses #17110

## Why

The app server installs its tracing subscriber during process startup, before `thread/start` resolves the effective config for the requested cwd. As a result, project-scoped `[otel]` settings from `.codex/config.toml` could be ignored by the app server even though the thread itself loaded that project config.

## What changed

- Added reloadable OTel log and trace layers so the app server can initialize telemetry from the first effective successful `thread/start` config without reinstalling the subscriber.
- Preserve tracing-opentelemetry span-context downcasting so inbound `traceparent` links and child trace headers keep working through the reloadable trace layer.
- Validate dynamic tools before reloading telemetry, then pin the process only after thread creation succeeds.
- Keep retired providers alive until app-server shutdown so existing sessions retain their metrics clients after a reload.
- Update global OTel metrics only after a replacement provider is built successfully, and clear metrics when telemetry is disabled.

items.body:
## Stack context

This PR is part of the cleanup for the merged agent identity stack.

Reference stack: https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/17387/changes

The old stack mixed three concerns:

1. the agent identity signing/encryption primitives
2. Codex task lifecycle and rollout/session task persistence
3. request authentication for programmatic Codex

The desired final state is smaller:

- shared agent identity mechanics live in `codex-agent-identity`
- Codex does not persist task ids in rollouts or session state
- programmatic Codex uses an explicit `AgentIdentity` auth mode
- each process allocates one runtime task id
- backend request callsites ask auth for a full `Authorization` header value

## Why

The task lifecycle design is the part of the old stack with the most uncertainty.

The old code created task ids around Codex threads, persisted them in rollout/session state, and threaded them through replay and resume paths. That made a temporary auth requirement part of core Codex history handling.

This PR removes that lifecycle layer.

## What changed

- Removed task id persistence from rollout and session state.
- Removed the core task lifecycle manager.
- Removed task id replay/reconstruction logic.
- Removed task id plumbing from thread/session state.
- Removed core-side agent task registration code.
- Kept normal ChatGPT/API-key auth working through the existing bearer path.

## Boundary

This PR does not add the new programmatic auth model.

After this PR, Codex no longer owns a per-thread task lifecycle. The next PR adds the replacement model: explicit `AgentIdentity` auth with one process task held in runtime memory.

## Tests

Tests: targeted Rust checks for core/session/auth rollback paths and CI.

## Summary

Fixes a race where a regular turn could emit `TurnStarted` before the initial user prompt was recorded. If the app interrupted in that window, core could persist `<turn_aborted>` without ever saving the prompt that started the turn.

This change queues accepted regular-turn startup input on the turn context, serializes startup transcript writes through a per-turn lock, and has the interrupt path drain that queue before writing the interrupted-turn marker.

## Root cause

The old regular-turn path recorded the initial user prompt inside `run_turn()`, after client-visible turn startup had already happened. The interrupt path could therefore run before prompt recording and append the abort marker to history first, or as the only item.

## What changed

- Add per-turn storage for startup transcript input and a per-turn serialization lock.
- Queue non-empty regular-turn input before spawning the regular task.
- Move startup prompt serialization into a shared drain helper that runs session-start hooks, user-prompt-submit hooks, prompt recording, and hook additional-context recording.
- Call the same drain helper from the interrupt path before appending `<turn_aborted>`.
- Add a deterministic regression test that asserts interrupted history contains the original user prompt before the abort marker.

## Validation

Passed:

- `just fmt`
- `just fix -p codex-core`
- `git diff --check`
- `cargo test -p codex-core abort_regular_task_records_prompt_before_interrupt_marker`
